title: The fleet, the contracts, and the price war
question: What does each AI-compute player actually own (which generation of silicon, on how honest a depreciation schedule), how long are the contracts that pay for it, and if the hyperscalers' surplus compute triggers a rental price war, who has the runway to survive it and who runs out of business?
finding: The 6-year depreciation schedule IS the neocloud's margin. On one-GPU arithmetic (H100-class, $32k installed, 80% debt, 70% utilization) CoreWeave's 6-year book life gives a full-cost break-even of ~$2.09/GPU-hr - profitable at the $2.35 market rate - but at the 2-3 year economic life the hardware cadence implies, break-even is ~$2.96/hr, ABOVE today's price: the reported profit is an accounting choice. The sector bought ~$18bn of disclosed earnings by lengthening server lives (Microsoft +$2.7bn FY21 +$3.7bn FY23, Google +$3.9bn FY23, Amazon +$3.1bn 2024, Oracle +$1.2bn, Meta +$2.6bn NI FY25 actual) while exactly one company shortened for AI reasons - Amazon, 6->5yr on a subset in Jan 2025, eating $1.0bn of net income - and the most honest books in the field belong to a neocloud, Nebius, at 4 years vs CoreWeave's 6 on the identical asset. The fleet census (ranges, flagged estimated) says who holds the melting ice: Voltage Park ~90% trailing-generation, Lambda ~70% into an IPO, Nebius ~65%, CoreWeave ~60% (the biggest absolute Hopper pile, ~250k units), xAI ~27% after the fastest dilution anywhere (was ~87%), IREN ~5-10% (bought late = newest fleet, pre-sold to Microsoft with 20% prepayment). The contract book (22 deals, filing-confirmed where possible) reveals a structural inversion: the GPU-owners' revenue mega-contracts all expire 2030-2032 (CoreWeave-OpenAI Oct 2030/May 2031, CoreWeave-Meta Dec 2031/Dec 2032, Nebius and IREN ~2031; CoreWeave's weighted-average REMAINING tenor ~35 months) while the landlords' leases run to 2036-2042 - the lease outlives the revenue that backs the tenant - and the landlord tier splits into insured (TeraWulf, Cipher, Hut 8: Google financial backstops on the Fluidstack leases, equity warrants as the price) versus naked (Applied Digital, Core Scientific: 12-15yr leases on unbacked CoreWeave credit). Headline deal sizes are softer than they look: both SpaceX leases (Anthropic $1.25bn/mo, Google $920m/mo) are 90-day cancellable - Google's right goes live Dec 31, 2026, the first dated tell. The price war, if it comes, is asymmetric by construction: cash floors are ~$0.94/GPU-hr for a 5%-money hyperscaler vs ~$1.22 for a 9.75%-debt neocloud, so at -60% the hyperscaler treads water while the neocloud loses ~$0.28 on every GPU-hour before depreciation; there is no price at which the levered neocloud wins a war the FCF-positive players (Meta +$46bn/yr) are willing to fight - and it does not need to start to matter, because it caps every renewal negotiation on the 2030-32 wall. Runway ranks the casualty order (Q1-2026 filings): CoreWeave ~2.3 quarters of simple runway against a $15.5bn 2026-28 maturity wall ($6.1bn remaining 2026) with covenant relief already granted in a bull market (DSCR test pushed to Oct 2027, minimum liquidity cut to $100m, unlimited equity cures to Oct 2026); Cipher ~2.2 quarters with $1.05bn amortizing; Hut 8 $160m cash and a BTC-collateralized loan (margin call 130%, liquidation 105% - an AI landlord whose runway is BTC-price-linked); versus Nebius $9.3bn cash and nothing due before 2029 (~43 quarters, prepayment-flattered) and Core Scientific ~22 quarters pro forma. Survivorship grid: price-setters (hyperscalers, SpaceX/xAI) win either way; Nebius is the best-positioned pure-play (most cash, no maturities, honest books); IREN the cleanest asset story; the insured landlords survive if Google's backstops hold; the naked landlords are CoreWeave credit in landlord costume; CoreWeave is the most structurally exposed large player (all three clocks - silicon, contract, debt - misaligned at once, offset by a $99.4bn backlog, 15-25% TCV prepayments and the Nvidia utilization backstop, which floors utilization but NOT price); and 'runs out of business' starts at the sub-scale spot-exposed Hopper fleets plus Fluidstack, a tiny counterparty carrying $10bn+ of obligations. Steelmen carried: 6 years may be defensible if old GPUs sweat on inference; scarcity may outrun the war; the backstops may hold - all three stretch the timeline, none flips the ordering. Converges independently with study 30's simulation (financing refusal, neoclouds first, 2027-28 window). Watch: Google's SpaceX cancel window (Dec 31, 2026), CoreWeave's first DSCR test (Oct 31, 2027), and the H100/B200 one-year contract rate. Builds on studies 36, 35, 27, 30.
